text: My wife paints with a palette knife, for the love of it. Every painting starts the same way: an empty wall, and three guesses.
Will it work on that wall? Which colors do I mix? How much paint will it take? Guess wrong, and you find out with paint already on the canvas.
So I built her a studio co-pilot. From an empty repo, during this hackathon.
A request goes in, typed or dictated, with a photo of the wall. Muse Spark reads it, and recommends a size and where it hangs. Muse Image paints three concepts, on that actual wall.
Don't like a shape? Tap it, and say what to change. Muse Image repaints only what you tapped. Every answer is a version you can keep, or go back from.

Then the picture becomes a plan. A band map is read straight off the painting. Each band's area becomes grams of paint and paste. And each color becomes a recipe in parts, from common tubes, searched with the Mixbox paint model.
Tick what's already in the studio, and you see what's left to buy.
Muse Spark writes the steps, and the app draws the canvas at every stage, so there's always a picture to paint towards.
Is this mix right? Photograph the bowl. The color is measured against the recipe, and it says which tube to add, and how much.
On a photo of the whole canvas, SAM 3.1 finds the corners, and every band is checked for coverage and color against the plan.
Four Meta models. One real painting. Built during this hackathon, and painted by my wife. Judges, it's live. Go try it.
